Fit chromatographic peaks

Source: R/fit_peaks.R
fit_peaks.Rd

Peak parameters are estimated by fitting one of several models to the data using nonlinear least squares (nlsLM). Supported models include Gaussian, bidirectional exponentially modified Gaussian, or exponential-Gaussian hybrid functions. The area under each fitted curve is estimated using trapezoidal approximation.

Usage

fit_peaks(
  x,
  lambda,
  pos = NULL,
  sd_max = NULL,
  fit = c("egh", "bemg", "gaussian", "raw"),
  max_iter = 1000,
  estimate_purity = FALSE,
  purity_args = list(),
  noise_variance = NULL,
  baseline = c("none", "flat", "sloped"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A single chromatogram in matrix format.

lambda

Wavelength at which to fit peaks. Must correspond to a wavelength present in x.

pos

A data.frame of peak apices and boundaries, as returned by find_peaks, with columns pos, lower and upper giving row indices of x. If NULL (the default), find_peaks is run on x at lambda.

sd_max

Deprecated. Filter peaks by width with filter_peaks instead. If supplied, it is applied as a cutoff on FWHM of 2.355 * sd_max timepoints.

fit

Peak model. Options are bidirectional exponentially modified Gaussian ("bemg"), exponential-Gaussian hybrid ("egh"), "gaussian", or "raw". "raw" integrates the signal directly by trapezoidal approximation without fitting a model. Defaults to "egh". See Peak models in get_peaks.

max_iter

Maximum number of iterations to use in nonlinear least squares peak-fitting. Defaults to 1000.

estimate_purity

Logical. Whether to estimate purity. Defaults to FALSE, and is always FALSE when x holds a single wavelength.

purity_args

A named list of additional arguments passed to get_purity, e.g. list(background_correction = "none", metric = "max"). A lambdas element here selects the wavelengths used to compare spectra, not the wavelengths at which peaks are integrated.

noise_variance

Variance of noise, passed to get_purity. If not provided, it is estimated once for the whole chromatogram rather than once per peak.

baseline

Whether to measure each peak above a local baseline: "none" (the default), "flat" or "sloped". See Local baselines in get_peaks.

...

Additional arguments passed to find_peaks, such as smooth_window, smooth_type, min_prominence_snr, min_curvature and min_amplitude. See Choosing the smoothing window in find_peaks.

Value

A data.frame with one row per peak and the following columns:

  • rt: Apex of the fitted peak model, or of the detected peak when fit = "raw".

  • start: Peak start.

  • end: Peak end.

  • sd: Standard deviation of the Gaussian component of the fitted model, which is not the width of the peak unless fit = "gaussian". NA when fit = "raw".

  • tau: Exponential decay constant (only when fit = "egh").

  • tau_right: Time constant of the exponential tail on the right side of the peak, the reciprocal of its fitted rate (only when fit = "bemg").

  • tau_left: Time constant of the exponential tail on the left side of the peak, the reciprocal of its fitted rate (only when fit = "bemg").

  • h: The amplitude parameter of the fitted BEMG shape function. It scales the shape but is neither its value at center nor the peak height (only when fit = "bemg").

  • center: The center parameter of the fitted BEMG shape function, the location around which the exponential tails are applied. May differ from rt (only when fit = "bemg").

  • FWHM: The full width at half maximum of the peak, comparable across values of fit. NA for a "raw" peak whose integration window does not fall below half its height on both sides.

  • height: Peak height above the fitted baseline.

  • area: Peak area above the fitted baseline.

  • r.squared: Coefficient of determination (\(R^2\)) of the fitted curve over the peak window, 1 - SS_res / SS_tot. Negative when the fit is worse than a flat line at the mean. Not returned when fit = "raw".

  • purity: The spectral purity of peak as assessed by get_purity.

  • window_limited: 1 if a fitted shape parameter hit a limit set by the integration window, or a "gaussian" or "egh" fit narrowed to one sampling interval at half height, meaning the window or the sampling rather than the data determined the reported shape, and 0 otherwise. Not returned when fit = "raw".

  • converged: 1 if the optimizer reported convergence for the final step of the fit, and 0 otherwise, including when part or all of the fit was skipped or failed (see Fitting procedure in get_peaks). Not returned when fit = "raw".

  • floor: Constant baseline offset (only when baseline = "flat").

  • floor_start: Baseline level at the left edge of the peak window (only when baseline = "sloped").

  • floor_end: Baseline level at the right edge of the peak window (only when baseline = "sloped"). The table is in index units rather than retention times: rt, start, end and center are index positions; sd, FWHM, tau, tau_right and tau_left are widths on the index scale; and area is integrated over the index axis. get_peaks converts them to the chromatogram's time axis.

Details

Peaks that can't be fitted are dropped if they've been detected automatically with find_peaks. Otherwise, if the peak positions are provided explicitly through pos, height and area are set to NA and they are marked 0 in the converged column.

The peak models, local baselines and fitting procedure are described in get_peaks, under Peak models, Local baselines and Fitting procedure.

Note

The loop over peaks in fit_peaks is adapted from the fitpeaks function in Ron Wehrens' alsace package. The Gaussian peak shape and the interface of the internal fitting functions are adapted from Robert Morrison's DuffyTools package.

References

  • Lan, K. & Jorgenson, J. W. 2001. A hybrid of exponential and gaussian functions as a simple model of asymmetric chromatographic peaks. Journal of Chromatography A 915:1-13. doi:10.1016/S0021-9673(01)00594-5 .

  • Naish, P. J. & Hartwell, S. 1988. Exponentially Modified Gaussian functions - A good model for chromatographic peaks in isocratic HPLC? Chromatographia, 26: 285-296. doi:10.1007/BF02268168 .

See also

find_peaks, get_peaks

Author

Ethan Bass

data(Sa_pr)
fit_peaks(Sa_pr[[1]], lambda = 220)
